source.title: At-Grok Is Not Converged:A Measurement-Validity Audit for Grokking Representation Metrics

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures when embedding effective-rank compression occurs relative to test-accuracy grokking and argues that compression often lags rather than coincides with it. This refines and challenges the timing component of V2, using a different representation measure from mechanistic circuit or Fourier-progress analyses.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own effective-rank trajectories, compression times, and related representation metrics. It does not report training-accuracy saturation or a training-set-size sweep, so those aspects of V1 are not tested. Cited results from other papers are not included as rows. The reported depth-law and free-decay findings are included as findings related to norm-controlled representation structure, not as tests of an efficiency account.
record.test_reason: The paper reports its own trajectories of a continuous representation measure, embedding effective rank, across the grokking transition. Two results bear on V2's claim that continuous progress measures anticipate the jump. frac-pre gives the share of rank compression done by the grok step. The grok-to-compression lag shows that compression continues long after the jump. This is only a proxy for V2: no Fourier circuit, memorizing component or restricted/excluded-loss measure is computed. The at-grok-vs-floor transient rows test whether a snapshot is converged, a different question, so they are relinked to none. The record's 'challenges' label is not warranted. The paper's timing correction targets Yunis et al.'s claim that rank compression coincides with grokking, not V2. Some compression precedes grokking in every arm.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors name normalization, not grokking as such, as the variable setting the lag: adding LayerNorm moves frac-pre from 0.87 to 0.25. Add also that a pre-registered control rejected per-token scale invariance as the cause. The authors state no mechanistic claim about why compression lags grokking.
record.recipe_differences: Uses squared-normalized embedding effective rank and long-trajectory compression clocks rather than identifying Fourier circuits or mechanistic progress measures. It separates test-accuracy onset from the point at which rank approaches its floor; the main comparison includes norm-clamped and free-weight-decay protocols.
record.method_sensitivity: Compression timing and the at-grok transient vary with architecture and normalization; frac-pre is 0.87 for the canonical transformer, 0.66 for the MLP, and 0.25 with LayerNorm. The lag estimate also varies with compression tolerance ε; lag/Tgrok ranges over [0.65, 1.46] as ε varies from 0.20 to 0.05. The norm-budget floor relation changes sign between clamp and free-decay protocols.

fits_no_version.finding: Embedding effective rank read at the grok step overstates the converged floor. The overstatement is 3–5× on the modular MLP, 2–7× under free decay including parity, and 1.3–1.5× on the transformer. It holds across participation ratio and stable rank.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representation-complexity metrics read at the grokking transition are transient and not the converged circuit's values.

fits_no_version.finding: The norm-budget/converged-floor depth law is Spearman −1.0 on the MLP clamp. It does not hold on the transformer and reverses under free weight decay.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Any relation between norm budget and converged representation depth is architecture- and protocol-specific.

fits_no_version.finding: Per-token RMS normalization on the embedding does not reproduce LayerNorm's deferral of compression (frac-pre 0.90).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization type modulates how far representation compression follows the grokking jump; input scale invariance alone does not.

record.problems: The one-variable architecture harness uses few seeds and a 6 × 104-step budget; the paper cautions that its largest transient magnitude (≈ 3.2× for the LayerNorm transformer) is low-powered. The transformer sweep has seed-fragile generalization: 16 of 21 clamp cells and 14 of 18 free-decay cells reach 0.90 test accuracy, with some clean cells based on one generalizing seed. Compression-time ordering is not established by the reported correlations. The converged floor itself can undergo a later collapse in low-budget MLP cells, so long training alone does not guarantee a stable reference floor.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for all individual transformer loci and spectral metrics beyond the reported aggregates; the text reports those collectively, with the largest locus transient stated as up to 3.6×. The audit's adversarial software test cases and cited prior-study results are not model-behavior findings.

untested.parts: No training-accuracy saturation curves and no training-set-size sweep are reported.
No Fourier-circuit identification, no measurement of memorizing-component removal, and no restricted/excluded-loss progress measures. Effective rank is used only as a proxy.
No image, text or molecule data and no lazy-to-rich test. Norm budget orders Tgrok, but switching the delay on or off is not tested.
No circuit-efficiency comparison, critical dataset size or ungrokking.
No comparison of learned algorithms across runs.

missing.what: The norm budget strongly orders Tgrok (ρS = +0.90 mult, +0.85 add) but not Tcompress (+0.18, +0.29). This bears on weight-norm control of grokking delay.
Post-grok Spearman between global weight norm and embedding rank by arm: −0.80 LayerNorm, +0.70 canonical transformer.
Sensitivity of the lag to tolerance ε: lag/Tgrok 0.65–1.46, lag 10,500–25,500 steps.
Late second rank collapse in low-budget MLP cells (wd=0.5): rank goes from about 22 to about 4 as the weight norm doubles well after grokking.

record.verdict_notes: V2 is linked only through a proxy, embedding effective rank, which the authors do not tie to Fourier circuits. The paper itself cites Sivasankar: a Fourier circuit-synchronization measure leads grokking by about 1,700 steps, while rank lags it. Verdicts should therefore be read as weak, proxy-level evidence. The record's 'challenges' label was dropped. The lag contradicts Yunis et al.'s claim that compression coincides with grokking, not V2's claim that progress measures anticipate the jump. Single-author preprint; code released.

versions.untested_parts: No reported training-accuracy trajectory showing saturation before test accuracy rises, and no sweep showing that smaller training sets require more optimization.

Measures effective-rank compression, not identifiable Fourier circuits, memorizing components, or the specific mechanistic progress measures in the claim. Does not test whether those circuits or measures anticipate the test-accuracy jump.

No image, text, or molecule experiments, and no test of a lazy-to-rich transition. A parity task and architectural/normalization comparisons do not establish the broader claim about non-algorithmic data or switching grokking delays on or off.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data.

Does not test whether weight decay selects a more efficient circuit, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below that size. Norm-budget/floor correlations are reported but do not directly test this account.
No identification or comparison of algorithms learned across runs.
No controlled test of adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point/softmax artifacts.

rows.measure: Embedding effective rank at grokking versus converged floor; at-grok value is 3–5× the floor, median 3.3×. Fast-grokking cells fall from ≈ 50 to ≈ 7; the slowest budget falls from ≈ 10 to ≈ 4.
rows.value: Converged floor after long training, as described above
rows.note: Reported over the fully-generalizing budgets; the study says the at-grok value is transient and that compression continues after grokking.
rows.check: Measures snapshot-vs-converged overstatement (3–5×), not whether a progress measure anticipates the jump. Baseline and value are framed oddly: the at-grok rank is listed as baseline and the floor as value.

relation.reason: It measures embedding-rank trajectories and their timing relative to test-accuracy onset, bearing on V2's continuous-progress-measure clause.

tranche.reason: The study's own trajectories qualify the timing of representation compression relative to grokking, showing dependence on normalization and compression tolerance.

source_check.notes: Embedding rank is a proxy, not a direct measurement of generalizing-circuit formation or memorizing-component removal. Table 2 uses median per-cell lag ratios; Appendix B uses ratios of medians. The LayerNorm harness and transformer lag ordering have limited power.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Modular MLPs and the tested transformer/normalization harness
reader_labels.reason: Effective-rank compression is gradual but its timing relative to grokking varies by architecture and normalization: some compression is already complete by grokking, while substantial compression remains afterward (r1–r2, r8–r13, r15–r18). These measures do not establish the timing of Fourier circuits or memorizing components.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Embedding effective-rank compression in the modular MLPs and the LayerNorm transformer arm
reader_labels.reason: The reported compression clock follows the test-accuracy grok step by large lags on both modular MLP tasks, and the LayerNorm arm has only 0.25 of total rank compression completed by grokking; this challenges a claim that the measured progress anticipates the jump.
